title: Extreme Ownership
author: Jocko Willink and Leif Babin
blurb: Jocko Willink and Leif Babin led SEAL Task Unit Bruiser through the brutal Battle of Ramadi in Iraq. After returning home, they began teaching the same leadership lessons to companies. Each chapter pairs a combat story with a business case and a principle you can apply. The core message is simple and demanding. Leaders own everything in their world, including the failures of the people they lead. From there, the authors lay out what they call the Laws of Combat. Teams must support each other, keep plans simple, tackle one priority at a time, and push decisions down to frontline leaders. The book closes by showing that discipline creates freedom, and that good leadership means balancing opposing forces. It is a practical, no-excuses guide for anyone responsible for a team's results.

lessons.b: After a deadly friendly fire incident in Ramadi, Jocko took full responsibility instead of blaming others, showing that leaders must own every failure in their world.
